title: Cheapest cables to join four towns
hook: Greedy failed with coins. Should you trust 'cheapest cable first' to wire up four towns?

knows: a loop: a path that comes back to where it started
doesNotKnow: that for connecting a network, taking the cheapest cable that closes no loop provably gives the cheapest network

misconception: Since greedy failed on coins, it cannot be trusted to build the cheapest network.
objective: The learner can lay AB 1, CD 1, BC 2 (total 4) by taking the cheapest cable that closes no loop, and explain why no network joining the four towns can cost less.

claims.text: With cables AB 1, BC 2, CD 1, AD 5, AC 4 and BD 3, the lowest total cost that connects all four towns is 4 (AB, CD, BC).
claims.source: Demo.tsx bruteMin(): all 20 three-cable sets, minimum over those joining all towns = 4. Builder re-ran in Node: 4.

claims.text: Once AB, CD and BC are laid, BD, AC and AD would each close a loop.
claims.source: After AB, CD, BC all four towns are joined, so any further cable joins two already-joined towns and closes a loop. Demo.tsx joined().

claims.text: Joining four towns takes at least 3 cables, and the three cheapest cost 1 + 1 + 2 = 4, so nothing beats it.
claims.source: A connected graph on n nodes has at least n − 1 edges (CLRS B.5.1, Theorem B.2). Any 3 cables cost at least the 3 smallest costs, 1 + 1 + 2 = 4, and those 3 do join all towns.

claims.text: Cheapest first, skipping cables that close a loop, always gives the cheapest network (Kruskal's algorithm).
claims.source: J. B. Kruskal, 'On the shortest spanning subtree of a graph and the traveling salesman problem', Proc. AMS 7(1), 1956; CLRS (3rd ed.) 23.2 with Corollary 23.2.

claims.text: Unlike coins, a skipped loop never blocks a better choice later.
claims.source: Cut property / exchange argument (CLRS 23.1, Theorem 23.1): the cheapest cable across any cut is in some cheapest network, so a greedy choice can always be extended to an optimum. A refused cable joins already-joined towns, so it can never be needed. Contrast: coins 1, 5, 6 making 10 (coin-greedy-trap: greedy 6+1+1+1+1 vs 5+5).

recall.question: Three towns: XY costs 2, YZ costs 3, XZ costs 4. Cheapest cable first, skipping loops. What is the total?
recall.why: Take XY 2, then YZ 3: all joined for 5. XZ would close a loop and is skipped. Three towns need 2 cables, and 2 + 3 are the two cheapest.
